newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Arancia-Corn gets OK to transfer energy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Arancia-Corn gets OK to transfer energy.

text.p: Arancia-Corn Products, a maker of corn derivatives, said Thursday it signed a contract with Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission allowing the company to transfer electricity from one of its Mexico plants to another.
Arancia-Corn Products is a joint venture between the Mexican firm Arancia and Corn Products, a division of CPC International Inc.

With the signing of the contract, Arancia-Corn Products will be allowed to transmit energy that it generates at its factory in Queretero state north of Mexico City to another factory in Guadalajara, said Luis Aranguren, vice president of operations for Arancia-Corn Products.
"In this case we are going to move electricity from San Juan del Rio (Queretero) to Guadalajara," Aranguren told Reuters in a telephone interview.
